title: Nadaswaram
summary: The nadaswaram is a long, loud double-reed pipe of southern India. A heavy conical body of dark wood opens into a wide flared bell, with seven finger holes and five more plugged with wax for tuning. It is played outdoors in processions and at weddings, usually with a double-headed drum.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Six notes of the mode are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and the bell opens as it sounds.
The five wax-stopped holes lower on the body are not played.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Its big, bright tone is made to carry across a street or a field, which is why it leads the music of processions and weddings in the south.
